headline: Luka Doncic scores 43, Lakers stretch winning streak to 8 with 131-123 win over Suns
text: PHOENIX -- — Luka Doncic scored 43 points and the Los Angeles Lakers stretched their winning streak to eight games by holding off the Phoenix Suns 131-123 on Sunday. Los Angeles played without second-leading scorer Austin Reaves due to a bruised heel suffered against Milwaukee on Wednesday. It did little to slow down the NBA's top scoring team — through three quarters. The Lakers led by 31 late in the third quarter, but the Suns charged back in the fourth behind Collin Gillespie . He scored 12 of his 26 points in the final quarter and pulled the Suns within 126-121 on a driving layup with 1:05 left. Phoenix got no closer. Quentin Grimes banked in a 3-pointer with 34 seconds left and Doncic sealed it with two free throws. Doncic, the NBA's leading scorer, hit five 3-pointers and went 12 for 14 on free throws for his sixth 40-point game this season. Grimes went 5 of 6 from 3 to finish with 22 points. Suns leading scorer Devin Booker had 17 points, but shot 4 of 14 from the floor and missed all four of his 3-pointers. He did not play in the fourth quarter as the Suns rallied. Doncic showed no limitations after rolling his ankle against the Bucks, having a hand in the Lakers' first 10 points with eight points and an assist. Doncic was 4 of 9 from the 3-point line and had 25 points by halftime. Phoenix labored at both ends while falling into an early 17-point hole, but chipped away to pull within 64-54 at halftime. The Lakers stretched the lead to 20 in the opening five minutes of the third quarter and kept pouring it on before the Suns fought back. Up next Lakers: Host Charlotte on Tuesday. Suns: Play at Denver on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Darius Garland scores 27 as Clippers run win streak over Hornets to 17 with 113-105 win
text: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Darius Garland scored 27 points, Max Strus had 14 off the bench and the Los Angeles Clippers beat the Charlotte Hornets for the 17th straight time with a 113-105 victory Sunday. Derrick Jones Jr . and Isaiah Jackson each scored 13 points, while Keaton Wagler and Gradey Dick had 12 apiece as the Clippers overcame a 13-point deficit in the third quarter to win for the third time in four games following a 1-7 start. Coby White scored 21 points and Naz Reid added 17 for the Hornets, who lost for the eighth time in their past nine games and fell to 0-2 at the start of a four-game road trip. Coach Charles Lee was ejected when he received a pair of technical fouls in a 17-second stretch of the third quarter. The Hornets haven't defeated the Clippers since Nov. 18, 2017. Their last road win in the series was Feb. 28, 2009. While still awaiting the season debut of Brandon Ingram (heel), Los Angeles continued to turn things around after its poor start to the season despite being outrebounded 46-37, while taking 18 fewer shots from the floor than Charlotte. Christian Anderson had 16 points for Charlotte, which shot 38% from the floor on 92 attempts. The Clippers shot 55.4% on 74 attempts and were 51.6% from 3-point range. The Hornets led 70-57 with 6:23 remaining in the third quarter after a three-point play by White. The Clippers closed the quarter on a 22-10 run to take an 84-83 lead into the final period. The game was tied at 90 with 9:33 remaining when the Clippers went on a 10-0 run that was capped by a running layup from Dick with 6:57 remaining. Up next Hornets: At Los Angeles Lakers on Tuesday Clippers: Home against Utah on Tuesday ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Spurs win 12th straight while sending Jazz to 12th straight loss
text: SALT LAKE CITY -- — Dylan Harper had 31 points and nine rebounds to rally the San Antonio Spurs to a 110-102 victory over the Utah Jazz on Sunday, giving them their 12th straight win, while sending the Jazz to a 12th straight loss. Victor Wembanyama finished with 26 points, 11 rebounds, six assists, and five blocks for the Spurs. Stephon Castle added 20 points and nine assists. Keldon Johnson had 11 points and 10 boards. San Antonio outscored the Jazz 27-5 in fastbreak points. Mo Bamba scored 26 points, while going 6 of 6 from 3-point range, to lead Utah. Darryn Peterson scored 17 points for the Jazz. Keyonte George finished with 13 points and eight assists and Brice Sensabaugh added 14 points and seven rebounds off the bench. San Antonio trailed for much of the fourth quarter until Harper tied it at 100 on back-to-back 3s and then Castle hit a pair of free throws to put the Spurs up 102-100 with 2:30 left. Castle’s steal and dunk with 47.2 seconds remaining capped a 14-4 run and extended San Antonio’s lead to 108-102. Utah scored seven baskets over eight possessions, culminating in Mamba’s step-back 3-pointer, to take a 33-23 lead late in the first quarter. San Antonio erased the deficit before halftime. Castle scored a pair of baskets, then fed Harper for a layup, to put the Spurs up 67-57 early in the third quarter. Peterson scored three baskets, culminating in a pull-up 3, to give the Jazz a brief 70-69 lead in the third quarter. San Antonio followed that with a 10-0 run to go up 79-70. Johnson powered the run with back-to-baskets and assisted an alley-oop dunk from Luke Kornet . Up Next Spurs: Host Detroit on Tuesday. Jazz: At Los Angeles Clippers on Tuesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Tatum scores 32, Celtics set franchise history on the way to 131-94 rout of Mavericks
text: BOSTON -- — Jayson Tatum scored 32 points in 30 minutes on a night the Boston Celtics set a franchise record for its lead at the end of the opening period on the way to a 131-94 win over the Dallas Mavericks on Sunday night. Derrick White added 16 points and Jordan Walsh 11 to help Boston win its sixth straight and for the 11th time in 12 games. Tatum had 21 of his points in the third quarter, connecting on 6 of 9 shots and knocking down four 3s. He scored 13 straight points to end the period. Boston pulled its starters after that but still pulled ahead by 41 in the final quarter. Playing on four days’ rest, the Celtics sprinted to a 24-4 lead with White and Walsh responsible for 19 of those points. The lead ballooned to 42-9 by the end of the first quarter, the 33 points the largest first-quarter lead in franchise history. Zaccharie Risacher scored 18 points for Dallas, which lost its third straight and for the fifth time in eight games. Cooper Flagg added 17 points and had four assists but was just 5 of 15 from the field with three turnovers. It was the second consecutive loss at TD Garden for the Maine native and reigning NBA Rookie of the Year. The Mavericks lost in Boston his rookie season last year in his debut against the team he grew up watching as a kid. Mavericks guard and former Celtic Kyrie Irving sat out for management of his left knee, which he had surgery on last March. He played 37 minutes in Dallas’ loss at Cleveland on Saturday. Boston’s cushion was as high as 35 points in the second quarter. Boston also had a 46-point lead at Charlotte on Nov. 6 and a 40-point advantage in its home matchup with Chicago on Oct. 26. The Mavericks, who lost in Cleveland on Saturday, looked sluggish throughout the opening period Sunday, missing 16 of their 18 field goal attempts and going 0 for 8 from the 3-point line. By contrast, Boston shot 59% and knocked down seven 3s. Up next Mavericks: Visit Golden State on Wednesday. Celtics: Host Magic on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Brunson hits tiebreaking 3-pointer in OT, Knicks earn 14th straight win over slumping Raptors
text: TORONTO -- — Jalen Brunson made a tiebreaking 3-pointer with 33 seconds remaining in overtime and the New York Knicks beat Toronto 112-108 on Sunday night, their 14th straight win over the Raptors. Brunson scored 28 points, and Karl-Anthony Towns had 28 points and 17 rebounds for the Knicks, who trailed by 13 points in the fourth quarter. Landry Shamet scored 23 points and OG Anunoby had 21 against his former team as the defending NBA champions snapped a two-game losing streak. Scottie Barnes scored 30 points and Jamal Shead added 19 but the Raptors lost their fourth straight and seventh in nine. Toronto has led by double digits in each of its past three defeats. The Raptors couldn’t hold a 22-point lead against Boston on Wednesday, and blew a 17-point edge at Philadelphia on Thursday. Immanuel Quickley scored 17 points, RJ Barrett had 14 and Jakob Poeltl 11. Collin Murray-Boyles had a season-high 13 rebounds for the Raptors. Barnes returned after missing four games because of a strained left groin, but Toronto fell to 3-8 in 11 games without Kawhi Leonard , who remains sidelined because of a swollen left knee. The Raptors last beat New York nearly four years ago, a 125-116 home win on Jan. 22, 2023. The Raptors led 84-71 on Quickley’s 3-pointer with 8:55 remaining, but Shamet hit a tying 3 with 1:16 to play and Towns connected on a go-ahead 3 with 20 seconds left. Those were New York’s only two made 3-pointers on 10 attempts in the fourth quarter. The Knicks shot 1 for 7 from distance in the third. Barnes sent it to overtime by making a step-back 3-pointer with 13 seconds remaining. New York’s Josh Hart finished scoreless for the second consecutive game. Hart shot 0 for 5 in 26 minutes and came in only for defensive possessions in the fourth quarter and overtime. The teams meet in Toronto again on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Rockets blow out Wizards 147-119; hold Trae Young scoreless for first time in his career
text: WASHINGTON -- — Amen Thompson scored 26 points and Kevin Durant added 25 to help the Houston Rockets rout the Washington Wizards 147-119 on Sunday night for their fourth straight win. The Rockets also held Trae Young scoreless for the first time in his NBA career. He missed all five of his shots and had previous scored in all 511 of his prior career games with the Hawks and Wizards. Alperen Sengun added 19 points and eight assists and eight rebounds for the Rockets, who had a season-high for points. Alex Sarr had 24 points and AJ Dybantsa added 16 for the Wizards. Dybantsa was 6-for-18 from the field. The Wizards have now lost seven games in a row after a 4-3 start to the season. Their last win came on Nov. 2 against the Magic. Washington went back-and-forth with Houston for the first quarter, but dominant second and third quarters by the Rockets paved the way for the blowout win. They outscored the Wizards 37-23 in the second and 46-34 in the third to pull away. Houston also outrebounded Washington 55-36. The Rockets used an 18-8 run to open the second half and put some distance between themselves and the Wizards. The lead eventually ballooned to as large as 31 points during that stretch. The Wizards were never able to keep pace with a Rockets offense that was efficient from the field and steadily grew their lead as the game wore on. Houston shot 56.5% from the field in the first half and made 10 of its 20 3-point attempts. Thompson, in the first two quarters, was 7 of 9 from the field and made each of his three 3-point attempts. Up next: Rockets: Visit the Miami Heat on Monday night. Wizards: Host the Memphis Grizzlies on Monday night. —- See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Hawks erase 22-point second quarter deficit to hand Bucks 10th consecutive loss
text: MILWAUKEE -- — Nickeil Alexander-Walker and CJ McCollum each scored 20 points and Onyeka Okongwu had 16 and 11 rebounds as the Atlanta Hawks erased a 22-point second-quarter deficit to defeat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-106 on Sunday night. Jalen Johnson added 14 points and 11 rebounds and Corey Kispert had 14 off the bench for the Hawks (8-6), who had lost back-to-back games coming in. Kasparas Jakucionis scored a career high 25 points, Gary Trent Jr. had 18, Kyle Kuzma 14 and Brayden Burries 13 for Milwaukee. The Bucks (1-13) lost a 10th straight game and are off to their worst start in 52 years, when they lost 13 of their first 14 in 1974-75 without an injured Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, per Sportradar. Milwaukee’s last win came on Oct. 26 against the Indiana Pacers in Milwaukee. The longest losing streak in franchise history is 15 consecutive games, set during the 1995-96 season. The Bucks sprinted to a 37-18 lead after the first quarter, led by Kuzma’s 12 points. Milwaukee shot 58% in the period. Milwaukee built a 22-point lead early in the second quarter before Atlanta stormed back to take a 55-53 lead at the half on Dyson Daniels’ layup just ahead of the horn. The Hawks extended their run in the third, getting the lead up to 13, and holding an 87-80 lead heading the fourth. The Bucks were within three with under a minute left but McCollum's jumper with 17 seconds left sealed the win. Jock Landale (right hip inflammation) sat out for the Hawks, while the Bucks were without Ryan Rollins (illness) and Ousmane Dieng , who is set to have surgery Monday on a left finger he fractured in Friday’s loss at Orlando. Up next Hawks: At Oklahoma City on Wednesday night. Bucks: At Miami on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Gilgeous-Alexander scores 37 as Thunder beat Kings 125-103 to snap 3-game losing streak
text: SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 37 points in three quarters to help the Oklahoma City Thunder beat the Sacramento Kings 125-103 on Sunday night and end a three-game losing streak. Gilgeous-Alexander shot 13 for 20 from the field, 4 for 5 from 3-point range and made all seven free throws. He played only 29 minutes, perhaps the only thing keeping him from a second consecutive game with 40 or more points. He has scored 31 or more in his last three games. Rookie Aday Mara had 16 points and 13 rebounds off the bench for the Thunder, who led by 27 points. Ajay Mitchell had 14 points, and Isaiah Hartenstein pulled down 11 rebounds. Rookie Darius Acuff Jr . had 26 points and six rebounds for the Kings, who fell to 1-12 and are 0-8 at home. They fell to 0-6 on a seven-game homestand. Zach LaVine did not suit up for the Kings due to an illness. After trailing 25-11, the Kings managed to charge back to tie the game at 47 on a free throw by Acuff with 3:42 left in the second quarter. The Thunder ended the period on a 15-3 run to lead 62-50 at the half after eight lead changes. Gilgeous-Alexander had 21 points in 18 minutes at the break. Gilgeous-Alexander’s 3-pointer gave the Thunder a 91-76 advantage with 1:44 remaining in the third quarter. The Thunder opened the fourth on a 19-4 run while Gilgeous-Alexander was watching from the bench and he did not return to the game. Nique Clifford scored nine points in his return to Sacramento after the Kings traded him to the Thunder on Nov. 8. Up next Thunder: Host Atlanta on Wednesday night. Kings: Host Phoenix on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
